LESSON: READING 9.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION: POETRY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry, part of Strand 9 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we describe a poem? 2. Why do we read poems?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify components of a poem for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read poems based on the theme for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. answer questions from a poem based on the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate reading poems for personal judgement.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify components of a poem for comprehension,

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read poems based on the theme for comprehension,

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. answer questions from a poem based on the theme,

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate reading poems for personal judgement.

   Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaborate with peers to list components of a poem,

2. read poems based on the theme (giving advice on good leadership among learners) and give reviews,

3. discuss main issues raised in a poem based on leadership,

4. team up with peers to play a vocabulary game involving words related to the theme,

5. works jointly with peers to use digital devices to watch poetry performances,

6. work with peers to compose a poem taking into account the various components of a poem,

7. recite the composed pieces as choral poems during inter-class festivals while applying non-verbal cues. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaborate with peers to list components of a poem,
2. read poems based on the theme (giving advice on good leadership among learners) and give reviews,
3. discuss main issues raised in a poem based on leadership,
4. team up with peers to play a vocabulary game involving words related to the theme,
5. works jointly with peers to use digital devices to watch poetry performances,
6. work with peers to compose a poem taking into account the various components of a poem,
7. recite the composed pieces as choral poems during inter-class festivals while applying non-verbal cues. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner engages actively to read poems based on the theme and

gives reviews.

• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with digital technology when watching poetry performances.

Values:
• Unity: This is developed as the learner cooperates with peers to play a vocabulary game involving words related to the

theme.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits a self-driven attitude when discussing main issues raised in a poem

based on leadership.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is promoted as the learner is exposed to issues about leadership in the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on poetry to their learning of similar concepts in Creative Arts.
